canonical_source.behavior: Expose the Content Planner route for the current tenant; this closure is limited to route exposure and does not invent ContentPlanningService behavior that is outside the canonical operation row.

laravel_adaptation.behavior: A dedicated Laravel route renders the existing tenant workspace through CanonicalWorkspaceRouteController after authenticated tenant-context resolution and explicit tenant.view plus content.view authorization.

authorization.fail_closed: Guests cannot reach the workspace, authenticated members missing content.view receive 403, and a member of another tenant receives 404 during tenant-context resolution.

tenant_isolation.proof: Focused acceptance exercises alpha->beta direct route access and requires 404; the route exposes no user, site, content, or other resource identifier.

validation_and_degraded_states.invalid_or_foreign_tenant: fails closed through tenant.context without rendering the workspace
validation_and_degraded_states.anonymous: redirected to the Laravel login boundary

persistence_and_runtime.persistence: none added by this route exposure
persistence_and_runtime.retry: No internal retry; normal browser retry remains truthful because no mutation is performed.
persistence_and_runtime.audit: No business mutation is emitted by this route exposure operation.

acceptance_tests.coverage: canonical operation identity, explicit action binding, auth and tenant.context middleware, tenant.view/content.view authorization, authorized rendering, guest boundary, missing-permission 403, cross-tenant 404, and absence of direct resource-ID surfaces

terminality.basis: The canonical route exposure is represented by an explicit, tenant-derived Laravel route with deterministic authorization/isolation acceptance; no unrelated Content Planner business behavior is claimed.
